scope: 账号列表批量授权及当前请求内复用；查询请求合并；慢请求加载状态回归

measurements.method: 同一隔离数据库内逐账号角色与授权预览，对比批量预读；单次服务逻辑测量，非整页P95或生产环境基准

pending: 账号派生角色及活动职责筛选的数据库分页
大量人员候选的远程分页查询
其余业务模块数据库查询优化
全系统并发和5倍规模基准

accountPagination.status: common scalar filters use SQL pagination after initial metadata load; derived-role filters retain compatible fallback
accountPagination.fix: watch query parameter content rather than object identity to prevent refresh loops
accountPagination.remaining: initial metadata and derived-role query optimization; remote option queries; other business modules and load benchmarks

accountFirstLoad.implementation: First list request uses SQL pagination; independent admin-only filter-options endpoint; four immediate basic fields; aborted options preserve selected values; options failure can retry
accountFirstLoad.remaining: Derived role and activity predicates still use compatible full projection; large-scale concurrency benchmarks not completed

coreIndicatorBatchQueries.implementation: Annual list uses bounded window-selected report IDs; batch selected-month and as-of-month archived reports; unchanged historical query and workflow
coreIndicatorBatchQueries.compatibility: Serialized results compared to existing per-indicator history/effective queries, including ordering and frozen target values
coreIndicatorBatchQueries.limits: No measured production latency or concurrency claim; undated all-year list retains legacy path; metadata mapping queries not yet batched

workRecordProjection.implementation: Resolve visibility once and load ordered records once; removes repeated page counts and capability checks from advanced-filter projection

verification.compatibility: Ordered legacy page concatenation equals new projection for owner, other user, administrator and viewer; isolated database only

workRecordProjection.remaining: Full authorized projection remains; SQL predicate pagination and workload benchmarks are not yet implemented

workRecordSqlPagination.implementation: Optional paged response for year, month, owner, status, current department and own-record predicates. Same live visibility; SQL count and LIMIT precede materializing record bodies; no entry narratives or all matching IDs in response. Work-record page navigation uses this path.

verification.comparison: Same items, ordering, counts and clamped pages; unauthorized status codes remain unchanged

workRecordSqlPagination.remaining: Initial filter metadata and complex narrative/root/date predicates retain legacy projection; authorization still reads permitted ID metadata; no P95 or concurrency claim

workRecordInitialLoad.implementation: Remove unused authors HTTP dependency; connect query loading state to table and pager; push selected year into record projection before reading entries; reuse account query for owner departments
workRecordInitialLoad.limits: Only common paged record filters measured with synthetic records; complex filtering, other modules, SQL counts and full-system acceptance still pending

auditListBatchReads.implementation: Task audit list batches referenced files and active fourth-level goals in groups of 500 IDs. Shared projection preserves output fields, ordering and progress calculations. Audit filter department labels use a lightweight name-only query instead of department impact statistics.

verification.browser: Chrome (Edge headless launch exited before page checks)

auditListBatchReads.limits: Mapper call count is scoped to file/goal enrichment, not all endpoint SQL. Other audit query projections, global history aggregation, message pagination and module P95 remain pending.

auditHistoryAggregation.implementation: Aggregate latest handling time only for distinct source record IDs, in bounded batches; empty histories issue no aggregate query. Same action predicates and timestamp representation; no authorization or workflow changes.
auditHistoryAggregation.index: Optional task audit sub_id/create_time index with idempotent apply/check/guarded rollback; tested only in disposable synthetic schema, not deployed.
auditHistoryAggregation.limits: Source audit lists are still unpaged and other enrichment queries remain. EXPLAIN estimates do not establish endpoint P95; full-system concurrency acceptance remains pending.

budgetVersionAggregation.implementation: Budget version metadata joins one per-period MAX aggregation instead of a correlated lookup per row; year permissions evaluated once per distinct year within each invocation. Preserves legacy numeric type, fields, order, filters and current-version semantics.
budgetVersionAggregation.limits: Full authorized version metadata is still loaded before advanced filtering and pagination. Synthetic single-query timing does not establish endpoint or full-system P95. No schema or business-data changes.

roleAssignmentBatchReads.implementation: Role filters reuse bulk account policy preparation. Policy and assigned-role SQL reads are bounded to requested account IDs in chunks of 500 instead of reading all account policies for every page. Empty input skips enrichment; GET-request-local cache only.

verification.boundary: 501 distinct IDs plus duplicate produce two batches/four policy-assignment SQL reads; no list preloading in POST requests
verification.compatibility: Legacy role membership matches for disabled accounts, deleted accounts, disabled templates and changes using the same token.

measurement.scope: Single isolated service projection comparison; not endpoint P95 or full-system benchmark.

roleAssignmentBatchReads.limits: Role listing still evaluates all non-deleted accounts for assignment status; global responsibility sets remain. Other list pagination and full-system load acceptance pending.
roleAssignmentBatchReads.rollback: Revert this backend change and rebuild the prior backend when authorized; no schema migration or business-data changes.

operationDetailLookup.implementation: Dispatch operation detail by whitelisted source type and primary ID, using the exact shared list column projection and visibility predicates. Removes five full log-list reads and sorting on each detail request.

verification.compatibility: All five source types compared field-by-field and over HTTP against legacy allOperations output. Same-ID cross-source records, missing users, before/after JSON, deleted budget versions, nondeleted work records, unknown IDs and revoked admin access covered.

query_scope.old: Five full source-list mapper reads plus sorting
query_scope.new: One primary-ID source mapper read for a valid type; no log-list mapper calls

operationDetailLookup.limits: Operation lists still load full projections and change bodies before pagination; list SQL pagination and end-to-end P95 remain pending.
operationDetailLookup.rollback: Restore previous backend artifact when authorized; no migration or business-data changes.

operationListBodyProjection.implementation: Advanced operation list filters and counts use summaries without before/after JSON. After pagination, one bounded primary-ID batch restores the exact original full fields of the current page. Exports and legacy direct management listing retain their existing path.

verification.fixture: 120 logs with 8KB JSON fields; seven combined/date/missing/empty filters across first, second and out-of-range pages
verification.compatibility: IDs, ordering including equal timestamps, totals, field options and full current-page maps compared with legacy projection; mixed source types with identical IDs remain separate.

operationListBodyProjection.query_tradeoff: One extra indexed body query for pages containing ADMIN records; no body query for empty or other-source-only pages. Off-page change bodies are not read.
operationListBodyProjection.limits: All summary rows are still materialized for filters and count. Database pagination, large-scale endpoint latency and full-system acceptance remain unfinished.
operationListBodyProjection.rollback: Restore the previous backend when authorized; no schema migration or business-data changes.

operationSqlPagination.implementation: Optional SQL count and key pagination for exact module/operator/action/object-type and date-range filters. Hydrates only selected records using original per-source projections. Frontend uses it for page navigation after initial metadata load.
operationSqlPagination.compatibility: Falls back for text or missing-value filters, out-of-domain date bounds, and duplicate or null matched timestamps to preserve original stable ordering. Legacy calls and exports keep their existing response path.
operationSqlPagination.limits: Initial field options, text filters and tied-time lists still use the legacy summary projection. Benchmark uses synthetic rows and one administrator session, not full-system acceptance or multi-account load.
operationSqlPagination.rollback: Revert frontend and backend commits or restore previous artifacts when authorized; no schema migration or business-data changes.

sidebarRefreshCoalescing.implementation: Home-scoped refresh queues merge rapid business events, reuse active periodic reads and schedule one follow-up for changes during an in-flight read. Hidden pages skip scheduled reads, returning visibility refreshes both counters, unmount disposes queued work. Keeps 30-second polling and existing count predicates.
sidebarRefreshCoalescing.limits: Counters still fetch original notice and per-domain audit list endpoints. Dedicated SQL counts, error-state improvements and full-system load acceptance remain pending.
sidebarRefreshCoalescing.rollback: Restore the previous frontend artifact when authorized; no backend or database migration.

sidebarSqlCounts.implementation: Optional countOnly=true on original notification and four pending-audit GET endpoints. No parameter retains original lists. Notice count shares visible/stale-notice predicates. Admin audit counts use aggregates; normal-user counts group by object/year and apply the same scope intersection as PermissionResponseAdvice. No audit VO, attachment name/body or fourth-level goal enrichment for counts.
sidebarSqlCounts.compatibility: Deleted/current pending states, normal vs admin handling, current core mappings, unread recipients, stale notices, permission revocation and object/year scope match the original visible list. Invalid task file references preserve read-failure behavior.
sidebarSqlCounts.limits: Count endpoints remain separate requests. Normal-user object/year scope evaluation still uses existing permission reads. Only unread-count latency was benchmarked here; short synthetic batches are not full-system or multi-account acceptance.
sidebarSqlCounts.rollback: Restore matching previous frontend/backend artifacts; no database migration. Deploy backend with optional count mode before the frontend that uses it.

overviewTaskAggregation.implementation: Administrator task summary aggregates effective third-level yearly task counts and progress in SQL; shared metric packaging keeps labels, empty/null values, rounding, overlapping flags and original year-end overdue semantics. Non-admin scopes and analysis detail queries retain existing logic. Name maps load lazily and are reused only within one GET request.
overviewTaskAggregation.frontend_fix: Core initial list reads with identical parameters share the active first-load promise. Initial history/detail links wait for the current load to finish; post-initial refreshes retain fresh reads after mutations.
overviewTaskAggregation.limits: Other overview modules still materialize their business projections, non-admin task summaries retain scoped tree queries, and full-system P95/load acceptance remain pending.
overviewTaskAggregation.rollback: Restore matching previous frontend and backend artifacts when authorized; no schema migration or business-data changes.

implementation.administrator_summary: One SQL aggregate over the original is_delete=0 records; date boundaries use the existing Asia/Shanghai connection convention. Preserves achievement counts separately from all nine award quantities, null quantities, current status, missing-date warning across years and empty values. No history, body or name projections for this summary.
implementation.scoped_drilldown: Permission metadata limited to requested IDs, deduplicated and read in batches of at most 500. Reuses the original row-scope matcher. Account and leadership relationships reused only within this invocation, never across requests; ordinary canRead behavior retained.

limits: Non-admin summaries and analysis still materialize full achievement projections with audit-history subqueries.
Other overview aggregations and initial multi-module request latency remain unfinished.
Sustained multi-account load, full-system P50/P95, SQL scan counts and index acceptance remain pending.
overviewAchievementAggregation.rollback: Restore the previous backend artifact or revert this backend commit when authorized. No schema migration, business-data update or frontend runtime change.

implementation.administrator_summary: One SQL aggregate for installed permissions, canonical numeric/dot/comma/space ancestry and unambiguous active annual rows. Uses annual target/actual values only, preserves exact missing/zero/negative target handling, excludes directories and keeps code-prefix manual/automatic classification. No name or full business projections in the fast path.
implementation.compatible_fallback: Nonstandard ancestry (including Unicode/control whitespace) and duplicate active annual rows use the original projection. Never assumes MAX(year_id), merges duplicate annual values, or normalizes stored ancestry. Database without unified permission tables retains the original path.
implementation.scoped_drilldown: Requested IDs are deduplicated and read in chunks of at most 500. Uses the same original row matcher and requested year. Account, leadership and department-duty reads are reused only within one invocation; ordinary single-object canRead remains live. All list order and business projections are retained.

limits: Unusual ancestry and duplicate-year configurations deliberately retain full projection fallback.
Non-admin performance summaries and analysis still materialize full indicator/annual projections, although permission metadata is batched.
Core, budget and work-record summary data phases, initial multi-module request latency and other list pagination work remain incomplete.
Sustained multi-account load, full-system P50/P95, SQL scan counts and index acceptance remain pending.
overviewPerformanceAggregation.rollback: Restore the previous backend artifact or revert this backend commit when authorized. No schema migration, business-data change or frontend runtime change.

implementation.budget_trend: Reads selected-year active month headers and projected task/source numeric fields in batches. Empty years skip item reads; single-task mode skips source reads. Duplicate active month headers use original per-month sheet selection; duplicate valid task indexes use the original task query/order. No cross-request cache.
implementation.budget_overview: Selected-month summary/detail reuse already-loaded task/source values and original precision rules; do not load the entire year trend. Trend charts remain in overview only; the original budget page stays hidden.
implementation.record_eligibility: Build selected-year valid task IDs, professional IDs and participating department IDs once from the original validated catalog. Filter original account order using the same active-user, valid-department and professional rules. Existing task resolution, read-scope filtering, submitted records and frozen snapshots remain unchanged. Existing catalog/department caches stay request-local.

limits: Record summaries still perform original owner/record scope checks and materialize submitted-row details.
Core overview reads, other list projection/pagination work, initial multi-module loading and scoped summary aggregation remain unfinished.
Full-system P50/P95, sustained multi-account concurrency, scan-row tracing and index acceptance remain pending.
budgetAndRecordReadBatch.rollback: Restore the previous backend artifact or revert this backend commit when authorized. No new schema, index, migration, business-data update or frontend runtime change.

implementation.records: Overview and maintenance use bounded record metadata batches (at most 500 IDs) and synthetic-owner checks over preloaded current-account departments. The original global visible-record list now shares identity/leadership reads only within its invocation; source encounter order is retained. All use the original row matcher, including stored record year and draft owner/server capability checks.
implementation.core: Overview archive query projects only indicator/report IDs, frozen name/target/value and month. Keeps original mapping join, cutoff and month/archive-time/report-ID ordering. Indicator access checks use bounded ID batches rather than per-row queries.
implementation.frontend: Six module reads are scheduled with at most two in flight; same-generation duplicate reads share a promise, queued stale reads are skipped and active reads abort on year/month changes or unmount. A slow module does not block ready sections. Same-period refresh errors retain and explicitly mark old results. Year/month/account changes clear old context; permission denials clear corresponding data or all cards and the drawer.
implementation.error_metadata: Common request errors retain Error type/messages/auth redirects and add responseCode. Summary keeps legacy error shape and adds accessDenied=true for caught module scope denials so denied values are not treated as stale data.
implementation.test_harness: Named run directories and configurable frontend/backend ports avoid existing local services. Occupied ports fail before fixture creation; tests can select an independent state file and results directory.

loading_comparison.method: One synthetic administrator, current optimized backend, sequential paired runs, one warm-up discarded and median of five samples. API response timings only, not browser rendering, cold start, multi-account concurrency or full-system P95.

recordCoreScopeAndProgressiveLoading.loading_tradeoff: On this small current-backend fixture, progressive loading produced an earlier first API response but increased full-set API duration and transferred bytes: six reads replace one combined call. It improves independent rendering under slow modules; it is not an unconditional whole-page latency win. The combined endpoint remains compatible. Multi-account/load acceptance is still required.
limits: Task/performance/achievement/audit/message list projection and SQL pagination work remains partial.
Scoped summaries and record metadata enumeration still materialize their original source sets; no full-system aggregation or data cache was introduced.
Sustained multi-account 1/10/30-user and 5x-scale end-to-end P50/P95 acceptance, scan-row tracing and index acceptance remain unfinished.
recordCoreScopeAndProgressiveLoading.rollback: No update package or online deployment. When authorized, deploy backend before the matching frontend so module accessDenied metadata is available. Restore matching previous artifacts to roll back; no schema migration or business-data rollback is needed.
